_meta.description: Reference information for the 22 crops the bundled model can recommend. Keys are the exact labels the model outputs.
_meta.typical_ranges_note: typical_ranges are approximate value ranges for each crop in the public 'Crop Recommendation' dataset whose labels the bundled model predicts. They are reference data for a rule-based comparison, not agronomic prescriptions. The test suite verifies that the model predicts each crop at the midpoint of its ranges.
_meta.season_note: Season information reflects common practice in India, where the reference data originates. Local sowing dates differ.

rice.name: Rice
rice.summary: A staple cereal that thrives in warm, humid conditions with plenty of water.
rice.description: Rice is the staple food for much of Asia. It is usually grown in levelled, bunded fields that hold standing water for a large part of the season, although rain-fed upland systems also exist.

growing_conditions.climate: Warm and humid. Grows best between about 20 and 35 °C with high humidity.
growing_conditions.soil: Clay or clay-loam soils that hold water well. Slightly acidic to neutral soils are preferred.
growing_conditions.water: High. Lowland rice needs abundant rainfall or assured irrigation.

rice.season: Mainly kharif (monsoon) in India; also grown in rabi and summer where irrigation is available.
cautions: Water demand is high. Without reliable rainfall or irrigation the crop is risky.
Sandy soils that drain quickly are poorly suited to flooded rice.

maize.name: Maize
maize.summary: A versatile warm-season cereal grown for grain, feed and fodder.
maize.description: Maize is grown for food, animal feed, fodder and industrial uses. It grows quickly in warm weather and responds strongly to soil fertility, especially nitrogen.

growing_conditions.climate: Warm and frost-free. Grows best between about 18 and 27 °C.
growing_conditions.soil: Fertile, well-drained loam. Tolerates slightly acidic to neutral soils.
growing_conditions.water: Moderate. Sensitive to drought around tasselling and silking, and to waterlogging at any stage.

maize.season: Mainly kharif in India; also rabi and spring in some regions.
cautions: Standing water damages the crop quickly; fields need good drainage.
Maize is a heavy feeder and yields fall sharply on poor soils.

chickpea.name: Chickpea
chickpea.summary: A cool-season pulse suited to dry conditions and low humidity.
chickpea.description: Chickpea is a cool-season pulse that is often grown on moisture left in the soil after the monsoon. As a legume it fixes atmospheric nitrogen and can improve the soil for the next crop.

growing_conditions.climate: Cool and dry. Grows best between about 15 and 25 °C with low humidity.
growing_conditions.soil: Well-drained loam to clay-loam. Tolerates neutral to mildly alkaline soils.
growing_conditions.water: Low. Often grown on residual soil moisture with little or no irrigation.

cautions: Humid weather and excess moisture encourage fungal disease.
Frost at flowering can cause heavy losses.

kidneybeans.name: Kidney beans
kidneybeans.summary: A pulse for mild temperatures and well-drained, slightly acidic soils.
kidneybeans.description: Kidney beans are a protein-rich pulse grown for their dried seed. They prefer mild temperatures and are less tolerant of heat, frost and standing water than many other pulses.

growing_conditions.climate: Mild. Grows best between about 15 and 25 °C; sensitive to frost and to high heat at flowering.
growing_conditions.soil: Well-drained loam. Slightly acidic to neutral soils are preferred.
growing_conditions.water: Moderate and evenly spread. Does not tolerate waterlogging.

kidneybeans.season: Kharif in hill regions and rabi in the plains of India.
cautions: Hot weather at flowering causes flower drop and poor pod set.
Sensitive to saline soils and to waterlogging.

pigeonpeas.name: Pigeon peas
pigeonpeas.summary: A deep-rooted, drought-tolerant pulse for warm regions.
pigeonpeas.description: Pigeon pea is a hardy, deep-rooted pulse that tolerates dry spells well. It is frequently intercropped with cereals and, as a legume, contributes nitrogen to the soil.

growing_conditions.climate: Warm. Tolerates a wide range, roughly 18 to 35 °C.
growing_conditions.soil: Grows on many soil types provided drainage is good.
growing_conditions.water: Low to moderate. Tolerates drought but not waterlogging.

pigeonpeas.season: Kharif in India. Many varieties are long-duration and occupy the field for five months or more.
cautions: Waterlogging, even for short periods, can kill plants.
Long-duration varieties keep the land occupied for much of the year.

mothbeans.name: Moth beans
mothbeans.summary: One of the most drought-tolerant pulses, suited to hot, dry regions.
mothbeans.description: Moth bean is a low-growing pulse of arid and semi-arid regions. Its spreading habit covers the soil and it produces a crop with very little rainfall.

growing_conditions.climate: Hot and dry. Grows best between about 24 and 32 °C.
growing_conditions.soil: Light, sandy soils. Tolerates a wide range of soil pH.
growing_conditions.water: Very low. Suited to low-rainfall areas.

mothbeans.season: Kharif in arid and semi-arid parts of India.
cautions: Not suited to heavy or waterlogged soils.
Yields are modest compared with other pulses.

mungbean.name: Mung bean
mungbean.summary: A short-duration warm-season pulse that fits between main crops.
mungbean.description: Mung bean matures in roughly two to three months, which lets it fit between main crops. It is a legume and leaves nitrogen in the soil for the following crop.

growing_conditions.climate: Warm. Grows best between about 25 and 35 °C.
growing_conditions.soil: Well-drained loam or sandy loam with near-neutral pH.
growing_conditions.water: Low to moderate. Sensitive to waterlogging.

mungbean.season: Kharif, and spring or summer with irrigation, in India.
cautions: Rain at maturity can spoil pods and reduce grain quality.
Poorly drained fields cause root problems.

blackgram.name: Black gram
blackgram.summary: A warm-season pulse that suits moisture-retentive loam soils.
blackgram.description: Black gram is a short-duration pulse widely used for dal and fermented foods. It prefers soils that hold some moisture and, as a legume, adds nitrogen to the soil.

growing_conditions.climate: Warm and moderately humid. Grows best between about 25 and 35 °C.
growing_conditions.soil: Loam to clay-loam that retains moisture, with neutral pH.
growing_conditions.water: Moderate. Sensitive to waterlogging.

blackgram.season: Kharif across India; also rabi in southern states and summer with irrigation.
cautions: Sensitive to waterlogging and to saline soils.
Heavy rain at flowering reduces pod set.

lentil.name: Lentil
lentil.summary: A cool-season pulse that needs little water.
lentil.description: Lentil is a cool-season pulse commonly grown after rice or on residual soil moisture. It needs little water and, as a legume, improves soil nitrogen.

growing_conditions.climate: Cool. Grows best between about 18 and 30 °C.
growing_conditions.soil: Loam to clay-loam with neutral to slightly alkaline pH.
growing_conditions.water: Low. Often grown without irrigation on stored soil moisture.

cautions: Waterlogging quickly damages the crop.
Hot weather at flowering and grain filling reduces yield.

pomegranate.name: Pomegranate
pomegranate.summary: A hardy fruit shrub that tolerates dry conditions once established.
pomegranate.description: Pomegranate is a hardy fruiting shrub that tolerates drought and a range of soils once established. Fruit quality depends heavily on steady watering while the fruit develops.

growing_conditions.climate: Does well where summers are hot and winters are cool.
growing_conditions.soil: Well-drained loam; tolerates a range of soils including mildly alkaline ones.
growing_conditions.water: Moderate. Regular, even irrigation during fruit development.

pomegranate.season: Planted as an orchard crop; plants begin bearing after a few years.
cautions: Irregular watering causes fruit cracking.
Prolonged humid weather increases disease pressure on fruit and foliage.

banana.name: Banana
banana.summary: A tropical fruit crop that needs warmth, rich soil and steady water.
banana.description: Banana is a fast-growing tropical fruit crop. It needs warmth, deep fertile soil and a steady water supply throughout the year, and it removes large amounts of nutrients, particularly potassium and nitrogen.

growing_conditions.climate: Tropical and humid. Grows best between about 25 and 30 °C; damaged by frost and strong wind.
growing_conditions.soil: Deep, well-drained loam rich in organic matter.
growing_conditions.water: High and continuous through the year.

banana.season: Can be planted in most months where irrigation is available; a crop cycle takes roughly a year or more.
cautions: High water and nutrient requirements throughout the crop cycle.
Strong winds can flatten plants; windbreaks or propping are often needed.

mango.name: Mango
mango.summary: A long-lived tropical fruit tree that prefers a dry spell before flowering.
mango.description: Mango is a long-lived tropical and subtropical fruit tree. Established trees are fairly drought-tolerant, and a dry period before flowering generally improves fruit set.

growing_conditions.climate: Tropical to subtropical. Grows best between about 24 and 35 °C.
growing_conditions.soil: Deep, well-drained loam. Slightly acidic to neutral soils are preferred.
growing_conditions.water: Moderate. Young trees need regular watering; mature trees tolerate dry spells.

mango.season: Planted as an orchard; trees take several years to begin bearing.
cautions: Rain or high humidity at flowering reduces fruit set and encourages disease.
Shallow or poorly drained soils restrict root growth.

grapes.name: Grapes
grapes.summary: A perennial vine that needs dry weather while the fruit ripens.
grapes.description: Grapes are grown on trained vines that need regular pruning and a support structure. Dry weather during ripening is important for fruit quality.

growing_conditions.climate: Warm, with dry weather during ripening.
growing_conditions.soil: Well-drained sandy loam to loam.
growing_conditions.water: Moderate and carefully controlled, usually through drip irrigation.

grapes.season: A vineyard is a multi-year planting with seasonal pruning and harvest cycles.
cautions: Establishment cost is high and the crop needs skilled pruning and training.
Rain during ripening causes berry cracking and disease.

watermelon.name: Watermelon
watermelon.summary: A warm-season vine crop for light, well-drained soils.
watermelon.description: Watermelon is a warm-season vine crop that matures in about three months. It does best on light soils with plenty of sunshine.

growing_conditions.climate: Warm and sunny. Grows best between about 24 and 30 °C; damaged by frost.
growing_conditions.soil: Sandy loam with good drainage and near-neutral pH.
growing_conditions.water: Moderate. Reducing water as fruit ripens improves sweetness.

watermelon.season: Summer crop in much of India, also grown on riverbeds.
cautions: Waterlogging and prolonged humid weather encourage fungal disease.
Heavy clay soils are poorly suited.

muskmelon.name: Muskmelon
muskmelon.summary: A warm-season melon that needs dry weather as the fruit ripens.
muskmelon.description: Muskmelon is a warm-season vine crop valued for its sweet, aromatic fruit. Dry, sunny weather during ripening gives the best quality.

growing_conditions.climate: Hot and sunny. Grows best between about 27 and 32 °C.
growing_conditions.soil: Sandy loam with good drainage and near-neutral pH.
growing_conditions.water: Moderate early on, reduced as the fruit ripens.

cautions: Rain or humid weather near maturity lowers sweetness and keeping quality.
Poorly drained soils cause vine diseases.

apple.name: Apple
apple.summary: A temperate fruit tree that needs cold winters to fruit properly.
apple.description: Apple is a temperate fruit tree. Most varieties need a long period of winter cold to flower and fruit properly, which is why apples are grown mainly in cool, high-elevation regions.

growing_conditions.climate: Temperate, with cold winters and mild summers.
growing_conditions.soil: Well-drained loam; slightly acidic soils are preferred.
growing_conditions.water: Moderate and evenly distributed through the growing season.

apple.season: Planted as an orchard; trees take several years to begin bearing.
cautions: The model has no input for winter chilling or altitude. Apple is generally unsuitable for warm lowland areas regardless of the soil readings entered.
Late spring frost during flowering can destroy the crop.

orange.name: Orange
orange.summary: A subtropical citrus tree that needs good drainage.
orange.description: Oranges and mandarins are subtropical citrus trees grown for fresh fruit and juice. They need deep, well-drained soil and are sensitive to both frost and standing water.

growing_conditions.climate: Subtropical. Tolerates roughly 13 to 35 °C; sensitive to frost.
growing_conditions.soil: Deep, well-drained loam. Slightly acidic to neutral soils are preferred.
growing_conditions.water: Moderate and regular.

orange.season: Planted as an orchard; trees take several years to begin bearing.
cautions: Waterlogged soil leads to root rot and tree decline.
Frost damages fruit and young growth.

papaya.name: Papaya
papaya.summary: A fast-bearing tropical fruit that cannot stand waterlogging.
papaya.description: Papaya is a fast-growing tropical fruit plant that can begin bearing within about a year of planting. It needs warmth and fertile soil and is extremely sensitive to standing water.

growing_conditions.climate: Tropical. Grows best between about 22 and 35 °C; damaged by frost.
growing_conditions.soil: Fertile, well-drained loam with near-neutral pH.
growing_conditions.water: Moderate and regular, with excellent drainage.

papaya.season: Can be planted in several seasons; plants remain productive for a few years.
cautions: Even a day or two of waterlogging can kill plants.
Strong wind and viral diseases are common causes of loss.

coconut.name: Coconut
coconut.summary: A long-lived palm of humid tropical regions.
coconut.description: Coconut is a long-lived palm of humid tropical regions, especially coastal areas. It needs warmth, high humidity and well-distributed rainfall or irrigation all year.

growing_conditions.climate: Humid tropical. Grows best between about 25 and 30 °C with high humidity.
growing_conditions.soil: Well-drained sandy loam, laterite or alluvial soils.
growing_conditions.water: High and spread through the year.

coconut.season: Planted as a plantation; palms take several years to begin bearing and produce for decades.
cautions: A decades-long investment: palms take years to bear.
Poorly suited to cold or dry inland conditions.

cotton.name: Cotton
cotton.summary: A warm-season fibre crop that needs a long frost-free season.
cotton.description: Cotton is the world's main natural fibre crop. It needs a long, warm, frost-free season and dry weather when the bolls open.

growing_conditions.climate: Warm, with a long frost-free season and dry weather at boll opening.
growing_conditions.soil: Deep, well-drained soils; black cotton soils and alluvial soils are widely used.
growing_conditions.water: Moderate. Sensitive to waterlogging.

cotton.season: Kharif in India; the crop occupies the field for roughly five to six months.
cautions: Insect pests are a major risk and need regular monitoring.
Rain when bolls are open damages the lint.

jute.name: Jute
jute.summary: A fibre crop of hot, humid, high-rainfall regions.
jute.description: Jute is a bast-fibre crop of hot, humid regions with heavy rainfall, grown mainly on fertile river-basin soils. After harvest the stems are soaked in water (retting) to release the fibre.

growing_conditions.climate: Hot and humid. Grows best between about 24 and 35 °C.
growing_conditions.soil: Fertile alluvial loam.
growing_conditions.water: High, and a supply of water is also needed for retting after harvest.

jute.season: Sown before the monsoon and harvested about four to five months later in eastern India.
cautions: A nearby source of clean, slow-moving water is needed for retting.
Harvesting and fibre extraction are labour-intensive.

coffee.name: Coffee
coffee.summary: A shade-loving plantation shrub of cool, humid hill regions.
coffee.description: Coffee is a perennial shrub usually grown under shade trees in tropical hill regions. It needs well-distributed rainfall with a short dry spell that triggers flowering.

growing_conditions.climate: Mild tropical highland conditions, roughly 15 to 28 °C, with shade.
growing_conditions.soil: Deep, well-drained soil rich in organic matter; slightly acidic soils are preferred.
growing_conditions.water: Moderate to high, well distributed through the year.

coffee.season: Planted as a plantation; shrubs take a few years to begin bearing.
cautions: The model has no input for altitude or shade. Coffee is normally grown in hilly regions under shade trees.
A multi-year investment that needs specialised processing after harvest.
